senses.gloss:
Sthūṇā in the Rigveda^1 and later^2 denotes the ‘pillar’ or
‘post’ of a house.
1) i. 59, 1; v. 45, 2; 62, 7; viii. 17,
14; x. 18, 13 (of the grave).
2) Av. iii. 12, 6 (of the Vaṃśa, ‘beam,’
being placed on the pillar); xiv. 1, 63;
Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, xiv. 1, 3, 7;
3, 1, 22, etc.; sthūṇā-rāja, ‘main
pillar,’ iii. 1, 1, 11; 5, 1, 1.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 153.

Sthūri has in the Rigveda^1 and later^2 the sense of ‘drawn by
one animal’ instead of the usual two (see Ratha), and always
with an implication of inferiority.
1) x. 131, 3.
2) Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 2, 4;
iii. 8, 21, 3; Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa,
xvi. 13, 12; xviii. 9, 7; Aitareya Brāh-
maṇa, v. 30, 6; Satapatha Brāhmaṇa,
xiii. 3, 3, 9, etc.
